verdict: ServiceNow grew revenue 20.5% to $4.1B and customers have pre-committed another $29.7B of future business, but GAAP profit fell to $277M as AI delivery costs surged and interest on new debt kicked in.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Software subscriptions — companies paying to run their workflows on ServiceNow, increasingly including its AI agents. 97% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Implementation help and training — people who set the platform up for customers.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to big companies — the largest running cost.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Growth held above 20%
takeaways.text: Subscription revenue grew 21% and contracted-but-not-yet-delivered revenue (RPO) reached $29.7B, up 22% — much of the next few years' growth is already pre-sold.

takeaways.title: AI deals are the new engine
takeaways.text: ServiceNow raised its 2026 target for AI net new contract value to $1.7B, the second raise this year — AI agents are becoming a real product line, not a demo.

takeaways.title: Two very different profits
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.27; excluding stock pay and one-offs it was $1.00. Stock-based pay is the single biggest gap between the two profit measures.

oneTimers: Interest expense jumped to $81M from $6M a year ago after ServiceNow issued new debt — a big reason GAAP profit fell even as revenue grew 20.5%.
Stock-based compensation was $633M in the quarter — the main reason non-GAAP net income ($1,039M) is nearly 4× the GAAP figure ($277M). The cost is real; it is paid in shares instead of cash.
Subscription delivery costs rose 58% YoY (to $1,054M) as AI features run on expensive computing capacity — GAAP gross margin narrowed from 77% to 71%.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted to −$15M: $69M of interest earned on cash, minus $81M of interest on debt and $3M of other costs.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
